quote: It is never shrunk to fit a website section.
gap: The skill holds the first half of the lesson well: don't turn a builder into form chapters. It has a classification gate, a written quality bar, a vertical slice, a full-screen route and an anti-pattern. It does not hold the second half. The 3D Studio, even after a fidelity pass, lost to a "game-like experiment (illustrated art, immediate feedback, a coherent little world)". gap: The skill has a 3D menu with measured sizes (model-viewer, three.js, R3F, OGL, Babylon, Spline) and one charts-only threshold ("many small SVG charts of ≤ 1–2k points are fine"). It has no decision between DOM/CSS, SVG, Canvas 2D, Canvas in a Worker (OffscreenCanvas), PixiJS, Phaser, three/R3F or a full engine (PlayCanvas, Godot or Unity web export). gap: The licence method is solid: classes A–D, trust the shipped LICENSE over the package field, keep a CREDITS.md. The 3D line is correct. Game-asset sources are missing: OpenGameArt (per-asset GPL, CC BY-SA or OGA-BY, attribution text required), itch.io packs (custom terms per creator, often paid, no redistribution, no AI), Quaternius, ambientCG (CC0 PBR textures), Mixamo (Adobe terms), Freesound (CC0, BY or BY-NC per sound) and Fab/Epic. topic: Configurators (vehicles, shoes, furniture, food, avatars): options, constraints, live price, persistence, mobile

quote: Keep it in the URL and in local storage, and audit mid-configuration states by seeding them with `--storage`.
gap:
There is real substance for made-to-order goods, all from one bakery project: the dependency graph sets the disclosure order, the customer's words beat trade terms, options are shown as pictures of that option, the preview is pinned on phones, prices come only from the owner's numbers, and choices survive in the URL and local storage. Car, shoe, furniture, food and avatar configurators also need:
- Constraint UX for incompatible options: hide, disable with a reason, or auto-resolve with a visible notice and undo.
- A rules and variant model: option → SKU mapping, and a versioned configuration schema so saved and shared links survive catalogue changes.
- A preview asset strategy: layered 2D compositing vs pre-rendered permutations vs real-time 3D, with the combinatorics and budget of each.
- Live-price mechanics: breakdown, delta per option, tax and currency.
- Save, share and compare.
- Swatches built as radio groups with names, not colour alone.
- Drop-off measured per chapter.
risk: A furniture or car configurator ships with options that silently invalidate earlier picks and share links that break after a catalogue change. Its image permutations blow the asset budget, and its swatches are unusable by screen-reader and colour-blind users.

topic: Undo/redo architecture (command pattern, snapshots, patches, event sourcing)
where: ui-ux.md §7b ('One history entry per gesture'); realtime-3d.md §7 (a template replacement goes through the same undo history); app-ui.md §7b and §10 (optimistic updates with undo; offline actions undoable). No architecture anywhere.
quote: Record the undo point when a drag or slider gesture starts, update without history while it moves, and commit on release, so one undo reverses the whole gesture.
gap:
The skill requires undo in several places but never says how to build a history.
- It offers no choice between command objects (do/undo pairs), full snapshots, structural sharing, Immer patches with inverse patches, or event sourcing, nor their memory and correctness trade-offs.
- It has no rules for what enters history: selection-only changes neither add a step nor clear redo; undo restores selection and viewport; when the redo stack is cleared; history limits; transactions that group actions; remote or collaborative changes kept out of the local stack; history kept across reloads.
The repo's research/stage2/experiments/S5-configurators-editors already benchmarks naive snapshots, Immer patches, Immutable and Yjs strategies behind one interface, with excalidraw and tldraw selection rules. None of it is in the skill.
risk: Undo that reverts only the selection, loses redo on a click, breaks after a template swap, grows memory without bound on big scenes, or corrupts state when a remote change interleaves. None of these shows in a screenshot or in the critique.

gap: The gates are decision-grade for effects on pages: a job per animation, a written reason per purpose-gated technique, 3D only with a real asset and every fact also in text, never a dependency for what CSS can do, a requirements table before scaffolding. What is missing is a requirement-first choice of rendering technology for interactive products (DOM, SVG, Canvas 2D, WebGL, illustrated sprites), driven by object count, fidelity, input, device and who maintains it. SKILL.md's knowledge-base table routes any 'configurator, builder or 3D viewer' to realtime-3d.md, which presumes 3D.
risk: A configurator that needed layered 2D images gets a three.js scene, with its weight, phone thermals and maintenance cost, because the only signature playbook is 3D.

topic: Moodboards and reference collection (vocabulary, inspiration vs imitation)
where: research.md (choose by problem; per-reference notes; take/leave; stop rule); art-direction.md §2 (style tiles, element collages), §3 (direction families as vocabulary); resources/inspiration.md 'Using references without becoming derivative'; templates/DESIGN.md References table
quote: The output is a short take/leave table, not a mood board to copy.
gap: Reference collection is strong: 4–8 references chosen by problem, a mix that includes one contrary reference, measured with dembrandt and audit.mjs, recorded as taken vs deliberately not taken, a stop rule, and no brand-clone files. Moodboarding is rejected rather than taught. There is no cross-discipline visual research (photography, film stills, architecture, packaging, signage, material samples) for building a visual vocabulary. Style tiles and element collages are named but have no template, size, tool or render step; compare.mjs --grid could build them but is never pointed at references. Boards have no annotation discipline saying what each image is for (light, crop, texture, colour proportion).
risk: Directions come from words and web pages only, so they stay inside web idioms and the model's prior. The style-tile step gets skipped or improvised, so the Phase 3 blur against the ledger has no real tile to blur.

topic: Curated inspiration sources per area
where: resources/inspiration.md (galleries, design systems, open-source products, craft writing); research.md reference mix; categories.md cites Baymard
quote: Mobbin | free tier very limited; Pro paid | real app flows (onboarding, settings, empty states), web and mobile | the best source for app *patterns*
gap: Good for app patterns (Component Gallery, Mobbin, Refero, Page Flows), marketing (Siteinspire, Land-book, Godly/Awwwards) and design systems and open-source products. There are no curated sources for the areas the skill claims to handle ambitiously: 3D/WebGL and configurators, editors and creative tools, game UI (e.g. Game UI Database), motion, typography in use, illustration, mobile consumer, and dataviz beyond FT and Datawrapper. research.md tells the agent to study 'ring and sofa configurators, invitation personalisation, tradespeople's quote flows' but names no source.
risk: For signature or niche work the agent searches ad hoc or from memory, lands on glamour galleries and imports spectacle, which inspiration.md itself warns against ('beware importing spectacle into products').

topic: Critique methodology
where: visual-qa.md 'Critique (Phase 7)' and 'Task walkthroughs'; templates/critique.md; SKILL.md Phase 7; audit.md §6 (heuristic passes, severity 0–4, cognitive walkthrough); lessons.md fresh-review row (research experiment L)
quote: A "yes" names a capture file and what in it shows the answer — and is then hunted
gap:
The method is strong: a first impression written before reading the direction; objective → element → effect → why; removal, swap and blur variants from capture.mjs and compare.mjs; evidence per answer; a required fresh-context reviewer; at most three rounds with re-scoring; walkthroughs with dead-tap counts. Gaps:
- Critique findings carry no severity (only the audit rates 0–4), so a cosmetic 'no' and a task-blocking 'no' weigh the same.
- The template has no row judging a signature route against its own experiential quality bar, and interaction feel is not checked from filmstrips.
- There is a single reviewer and no way to handle disagreement.
- There is no step with real users; the walkthrough is correctly labelled 'not a usability test'.
risk: Signature experiences pass critique without ever being judged against the bar they were built for, and rounds get spent on cosmetic 'no's while a serious one waits.

topic: Visual-quality evaluation without fake scores
where: SKILL.md commitment 4 and the Scripts section; visual-qa.md; templates/critique.md checks 12–14 and 22; compare.mjs --blur and --grid; capture.mjs --variant
quote: Scripts report facts, not taste. A clean audit is not a good design, and a signal is a question to answer, not a rule to obey.
gap: There are no numeric aesthetic scores. Judgements are yes/no/partial tied to named captures, plus squint (blur) sheets, removal variants and blurred comparison with past outputs from the ledger. What is thin is check 22 ('hold up beside the Phase 2 references in finish, restraint and hierarchy?'), which has no protocol: no same-width sheet beside the references, no pairwise comparison of candidate directions. Five-second tests and 'two people outside and two inside the market' are recommended, but the agent cannot run them and is not told to report them as not done.
risk: The one judgement about finish, beside the references, turns into opinion, and candidate directions are chosen by narrative rather than by a structured side-by-side comparison.

topic: Failure cases (redesigns that got worse, beautiful but unusable, over-minimalism, hidden navigation, 3D hurting conversion)
where: lessons.md (the skill's own failures); anti-patterns.md (refresh, prior, 'a site made only of type, rules and data fragments'); framing.md §3; design-theory.md A1 (aesthetic–usability caveat); responsive.md §5 and ui-ux.md §6 (hidden navigation, hamburger); motion.md §9 ('3D is decoration'); performance.md intro
quote: hidden navigation is used far less than visible navigation — show the top 3–5 destinations when you can and hide only the long tail
gap: The skill's own failures are logged thoroughly (30+ lesson rows), and several failure modes have rules: attractive-but-inappropriate, attractiveness masking real problems, hidden navigation, 3D as decoration, the over-minimal type-only site. Missing is the external canon a senior cites: documented redesigns that lost users or revenue and why (learned locations removed, signifiers lost in flat UI, ghost buttons, low-contrast minimalism, mystery-meat icons, hero carousels), and evidence on when 3D or AR helps or hurts conversion against its load cost. The operational defences are missing too: staged rollout, opt-in beta, A/B or holdout, post-launch metrics, rollback criteria. framing.md only asks 'can it be A/B tested'; Phase 8 plans no measurement after launch.
risk: The skill guards against its own past mistakes but can still ship a textbook redesign failure it has never met, and it hands off with no plan to detect a drop in conversion or task success after launch.

topic: AI frontend workflows (skills, rules, design-review agents, screenshot-to-code, browser automation)
where: SKILL.md Phase 7; visual-qa.md "Critique (Phase 7)" step 1; art-direction.md §2 (subagent directions); discovery.md §7 (CLAUDE.md, progress.md, todo.md); realtime-3d.md §9 (parallel agents); resources/tools.md "Detectors and review skills", "Browser tools for agents"; all Playwright scripts
quote: When a subagent tool exists, a fresh-context reviewer is required — a subagent given only the brief, the direction from `DESIGN.md` and the capture paths, state captures included.
gap: Two parts are strong and backed by evidence: the design-review agent protocol (experiment L) and browser automation, which runs through every script. The rest is missing. There is no screenshot-to-code or reference-to-code loop: nothing on giving the model a reference frame or Figma node and converging on it with an overlay or diff. There is no design-tool bridge: nothing on Figma or Dev Mode MCP, Code Connect, or pulling variables and components from the file; DTCG gets one line. There are no project rules that keep an agent on the system across sessions, such as stylelint or eslint rules against raw hex and px, or hooks that run audit.mjs on each edit. Nothing covers the limits of model vision: tall captures get downscaled, so small text should be read from 1:1 crops. impeccable, gstack /design-review, Playwright MCP and DevTools MCP get one line each, with no sign any was run.
risk: In a Figma-led project the agent rebuilds from screenshots it eyeballed instead of the file's variables and components, and the build drifts from the design. In later sessions new code brings back raw values that no lint catches. A "looks fine" verdict on a downscaled 390×12000 capture misses the 1–4 px and 12 px defects the skill says it checks.

topic: Screenshot-driven iteration loop across devices
where: SKILL.md Phases 6–7; visual-qa.md "Capturing reliably", "Verify the verifier", "Flows", "Task walkthroughs", "Critique" (bounded rounds); scripts/capture.mjs (grow/decode/fold/element 3×/variants), compare.mjs (sheets, blur), states.mjs (--each, tap rings, dead-tap detection)
quote: Fix and re-capture; do not close a loop on the assumption that a change did what you intended.
gap: Everything runs in Chromium with mobile emulation. lib/env.mjs launches only chromium, and responsive.md admits that WebKit descriptors are reused on Chromium. So the loop never sees iOS Safari (URL-bar and keyboard viewport changes, safe-area insets, which are 0 in emulation, WebKit rendering) or Firefox. There is no real-device step except for GPU work. Nothing says how to feed captures to a vision model, such as tiling tall full-page shots or judging 1:1 crops; "may need splitting" appears only for the report to the user.
risk: A layout signed off at 390 in Chromium breaks on an iPhone: a sticky CTA hidden under the toolbar or keyboard, or the notch overlapping the header. Tall phone captures are judged after downscaling, which hides the small misalignments the loop is meant to catch.

topic: Visual regression tooling (Playwright screenshots, pixelmatch, BackstopJS, Loki, Storybook)
where: resources/tools.md "Visual regression and comparison"; scripts/compare.mjs --diff; states.mjs (pixelmatch only for dead-step detection); visual-qa.md "Flows" (keep the walk as a Playwright e2e test)
quote: Playwright's `toHaveScreenshot` (in projects already on Playwright Test); pixelmatch + pngjs (in `compare.mjs`); odiff, reg-cli (MIT, Wasm-backed); BackstopJS and Lost Pixel (MIT; quiet since 2024).
gap: compare.mjs --diff is a one-off pixel count: threshold 0.1, no pass/fail exit code, no masks for dynamic regions, and when image sizes differ it silently compares only the overlap. Storybook, Loki and Chromatic are absent, and so is any component-state story approach. There is no determinism recipe: fonts awaited, animations frozen, clock and data fixed, one OS and engine in Docker, a baseline per theme and width. At hand-off the skill leaves an axe test and a flow test in the project, but no snapshot suite that locks in the new look.
risk: The redesign's look regresses silently in the next sprint. A diff between captures of different heights shows only the overlap, so content pushed down never appears. Any suite the user adds later flakes on fonts and animation and gets switched off.

topic: Responsive testing across continuous width ranges (not only 375/768/1440)
where: responsive.md §1 (intrinsic layout, container queries), §7 (which widths), §8 (the pass); web-design.md §4; capture.mjs/audit.mjs --widths lists
quote: Breakpoints go where the content breaks; for app shells align with window classes: compact < 600 · medium 600–839 · expanded 840–1199 · large ≥ 1200.
gap: The intrinsic-layout principle is right (Every Layout primitives, container queries, breakpoints from content). Verification, though, is at named widths only: 320/360/390/412/768/820/1024/1280/1366/1440/1536/1920. There is no sweep (for example 320→1920 in 10–20 px steps, running the overflow, clipping and nowrap probes at each step and capturing only where a probe changed). There is no resize-drag check, and no sweep of a component across the slot widths its container queries serve. The repo's research has responsive-sweep.mjs, but it is still 16 discrete classes and does not ship with the skill.
risk: Breakage lands at widths nobody captured: 900–1000 px tablets and split screens, 1100 px laptops with a sidebar open, 600–700 px foldables. That is where a two-column hero squeezes or a nav overlaps just before it collapses, and a container-query card breaks in a slot width no page exercises.

topic: Real-content stress (long/short strings, missing images, huge/negative numbers, localisation, 0/1/many, errors, slow network)
where: app-ui.md §2 (content extremes); visual-qa.md "The design QA matrix"; framing.md §5 "Reality"; audit.md §5; multilingual.md §1; states.mjs (route fixtures, delay, abort, status 500, offline); perf.mjs (throttling)
quote: Also render the **content extremes**: 0, 1, typical and 100+ items; 1-character and 70-character names; long words and URLs; missing images; large numbers and currencies; non-Latin text; RTL if supported.
gap: The list is right, and states.mjs can mock data states, but nothing generates the extremes. Missing: a pseudo-localisation or DOM text-injection pass (+30–40% expansion, accents, brackets); fixture recipes for null, NaN, negative, 12-digit, emoji and combining-mark values; a documented way to break images (aborting image globs works but is never shown); and global CPU or network throttling in states.mjs, which has only a per-route delay. states.mjs runs axe on each state but not audit.mjs's clipped-text and overflow probes, so a stress state is only as good as the eye that inspects it. CSS rules for surviving long content (overflow-wrap: anywhere, line-clamp with the full text reachable) are only partly there.
risk: A German label, a 70-character customer name or a negative balance clips inside a fixed-height pill in a state capture nobody inspects closely. The run still passes, because the clip probes never ran on that state.

topic: RTL and Arabic at component level (icons, breadcrumbs, forms, tables, charts, navigation, bidi, mirroring)
where: multilingual.md §1, §2, §2a, §4; implementation.md "RTL-ready"; audit.mjs + lib/inventory.mjs (digit mixing, numeric column alignment, type=number on RTL, untranslated strings); a11y.mjs (language of parts)
quote: Implement with `:dir(rtl) .icon-dir { transform: scaleX(-1) }` or the set's own prop (Phosphor's `mirrored`).
gap: Numbers, bidi marks, digit systems, calendars, numeric-column alignment and the icon-mirroring list are measured and excellent. Component behaviour beyond them is not covered: breadcrumb separators and prev/next pagination; APG arrow-key semantics in RTL (Left means next for tabs, sliders and carousels); translateX slide and drawer animations and box-shadow offsets, which logical properties do not flip; LTR data fields inside RTL forms (email, URL, IBAN, phone) and dir="auto" on user text; the direction of range sliders and progress; chart legend and axis placement beyond the time axis; carousel swipe direction. No script flags physical properties or unmirrored directional icons. The checklist asks for a capture "with `dir` toggled", but capture.mjs has no such flag.
risk: An Arabic build passes every script while chevrons, drawer entrances and tab arrow keys run backwards, and email or IBAN fields render as scrambled bidi text.

topic: Mobile product design (thumb zones, bottom nav, sheets, gestures, keyboard, safe areas, offline, iOS/Android conventions)
where: responsive.md §3–§6; categories.md "Mobile-first consumer", "Field and frontline tools"; app-ui.md §7b; ui-ux.md §6, §7b; technical-qa.md implementation checks; states.mjs tap/swipe
quote: Virtual keyboard: by default a fixed bottom submit bar stays *under* the keyboard. For forms with sticky actions, `interactive-widget=resizes-content` (Chromium/Firefox Android) plus the VisualViewport API on iOS.
gap: The web-mobile rules are solid: Hoober evidence rather than thumb-zone folklore, at most five tabs, 44 pt / 48 dp targets, safe-area CSS, inputmode and enterkeyhint, offline and freshness honesty. Missing: a bottom-sheet behaviour spec (detents, drag-to-dismiss velocity, nested scroll, iOS scroll lock); system back and gesture handling (a history entry so Android back or an iOS edge-swipe closes the overlay rather than leaving the page, and edge-swipe conflicts); PWA and standalone display-mode, and status-bar theming; a pull-to-refresh policy; haptics; where iOS HIG and Material patterns diverge. Every rule is verified only in Chromium emulation, where env() insets are 0 and no virtual keyboard appears.
risk: On Android, pressing back on an open sheet leaves the whole flow. Sticky CTAs sit under the iOS keyboard or home indicator, and the notch overlaps headers. All of this ships because the only test environment cannot reproduce it.

topic: Progressive enhancement and degradation tiers (strong, average, low-power, reduced motion, no WebGL)
where: realtime-3d.md §6; discovery.md §5b step 5; motion.md §6 and §9 ("Failure path"); implementation.md "The reveal, written safely"; audit.mjs no-JS and reduced-motion renders; motion.mjs
quote: Tiers change **resolution, effects and tessellation, never the look**: the same lights, materials and composition on every tier, so the lowest tier still looks intentional.
gap: Reduced motion and no-JS are implemented and checked (motion.mjs, audit.mjs); tiers are not. Missing: device-classification code (deviceMemory, hardwareConcurrency, the GPU renderer string, failIfMajorPerformanceCaveat); step-down thresholds (for example, p95 frame time over N continuous frames, with hysteresis); webglcontextlost and restore handling; Save-Data, prefers-reduced-data or Low Power Mode heuristics; a tier matrix for rich effects outside 3D (video backgrounds, backdrop blur, Lottie); a URL flag that forces a tier so each tier can be captured. "Start from a device guess (touch, memory)" is the whole of the detection guidance, and "if WebGL fails, keep the poster" gives no way to detect the failure.
risk: In practice a signature experience ships with one tier. Low-end Androids and phones in Low Power Mode get the high tier, stutter, heat up, and lose the GL context to a black canvas. No capture ever shows what the low tier looks like.

topic: Performance budgets for rich experiences (bundle, textures, memory, CPU/GPU, thermals)
where: performance.md §1 (signature column; pages around a signature product), §2; motion.md §9 (asset budgets); realtime-3d.md §3–§5; visual-qa.md "3D and WebGL experiences"
quote: Budget: ≤ ~1.5 MB GLB for a product model, textures ≤ 2048² (1024² on mobile).
gap: Bundle, image, font and texture budgets have numbers, and the KTX2-vs-WebP reasoning (16 MB decoded for one 2048² texture) is sound. Per-frame and device budgets do not exist. Missing: a split of the 16.7 / 8.3 ms frame between JS and GPU with headroom; caps on draw calls, triangles and materials per tier; a GPU-memory or JS-heap ceiling (iOS Safari reloads tabs under memory pressure); a sustained-load thermal test (a 10-minute run watching frame-time drift). Nothing measures these: the benchmark harness and "a build script that fails" are described but not shipped, and performance.md admits that requestAnimationFrame at rest and layer counts are checked by hand in DevTools.
risk: A configurator meets its transfer budget, then crashes or throttles on a mid-range phone after a few minutes of use. Draw-call and texture-memory regressions between iterations go unnoticed.

topic: Loading experiences (skeletons, progressive assets, staged scenes, how games hide loading)
where: app-ui.md §8; ui-ux.md §4; motion.md §5 "Loading", §6, §9 "Poster first"; realtime-3d.md §7 (poster → live hand-over); art-direction.md §4; performance.md §2–§3
quote: under 1 s show nothing — but *lay out* the skeleton from first paint (in the server or static HTML, `visibility: hidden` until 1 s), so the space is reserved
gap: Conventional loading is specific: time thresholds, skeletons shaped like the final layout, spinner delay and minimum display time, the poster as the LCP, warming on intent, no engine boot during a morph. Missing: progressive asset delivery (LQIP, blur-up or dominant-colour image placeholders; low-res textures or LODs streamed and then swapped); a staged scene boot (interactive shell → geometry → materials → post-processing, each reported); shader and pipeline pre-compilation (three.js compileAsync) to avoid hitches on first interaction; the game patterns for hiding load (give the player something to do while content streams, load behind a menu or camera move, progress weighted by bytes).
risk: The poster hands over to a canvas that hitches for a second or more on the first orbit while shaders compile. Mid-range phones sit through a long blank or spinner stage, and image-heavy pages flash empty boxes.

topic: Off-main-thread work (Workers, OffscreenCanvas, WASM)
where: performance.md §2 (the filters row) and §5; motion.md §7; realtime-3d.md §7
quote: Yielding once does not free the thread for the *next* input; chunk long work or move it to a Worker.
gap: scheduler.yield is measured (INP 376 → 24 ms), but Workers are only named. Nothing covers: when a Worker pays off (structured-clone cost against transferables); RPC helpers such as Comlink; SharedArrayBuffer and its COOP/COEP requirement; OffscreenCanvas via transferControlToOffscreen for 2D and WebGL rendering, and where it is unsupported; WASM for heavy compute (image processing, geometry, parsing); moving procedural geometry and asset decoding off the main thread. WASM appears only as a runtime size cost. The repo has a stage-2 lab, research/stage2/experiments/S1-rendering-lab (with a canvas2d-worker variant), that measured OffscreenCanvas in a worker, but none of it is cited in or distilled into the skill.
risk: Procedural generation, large filters and decoding block input; the morph that stretched from 0.56 s to 3.8 s is exactly this. INP fails, and the agent guesses at Worker plumbing without knowing what it costs.

topic: Product types coverage: SaaS, dashboards, ecommerce, mobile apps, white-label, POS, marketing, configurators
where: framing.md §1; categories.md (the dials and twelve playbooks); app-ui.md; discovery.md §5–§5c; realtime-3d.md
quote: Farm, warehouse, clinical, site, retail-floor and delivery tools: a phone or rugged tablet used many times a shift, one-handed or gloved, in glare, noise or cold, with patchy signal and constant interruption.
gap: Marketing, SaaS, dashboards, ecommerce, enterprise, docs, fintech, mobile-first web, field tools, content, public services and configurators each have dials and numbers. Three types are absent. White-label and multi-tenant products: per-tenant brand tokens with contrast guaranteed whatever colour a tenant uploads, logo slots, and what tenants may and may not theme. POS and kiosks: fixed landscape touchscreens, speed of service, cashier versus customer-facing displays, receipts, offline card fallback, attract loops, reach ranges for standing users. Native mobile apps: the skill is web-only, with one line on Konsta, Ionic and Capacitor.
risk: A white-label redesign hard-codes one brand's palette and fails contrast the day a tenant sets yellow. A POS screen gets either desk density or the field profile, and neither was built for a cashier with a queue.

topic: Typography including Arabic and numeric content
where: design-theory.md Part C and Part D (Typography); multilingual.md §2–§2a; resources/type-and-colour.md; performance.md §4; scripts/fonts.mjs (tabular figures per digit system, --fallback metrics); audit.mjs number checks; lib/saturated-fonts.json
quote: Write `ar-SA-u-nu-latn` or `ar-SA-u-nu-arab` — never rely on the region.
gap: Arabic vertical metrics are missing: harakat and tall ascenders get clipped by a line-height ≤ 1.2 or fixed-height pills, and fonts.mjs reports x-height and cap-height but not ascent and descent against the line box. Also missing: mixed-script baseline and line-height when Arabic and Latin share a line; Nastaliq for Urdu, whose vertical extent is very large; kashida versus justification; currency glyph coverage, such as the new Saudi riyal sign (Unicode 17), which needs a font that has it or an explicit fallback. No check detects clipped diacritics.
risk: Arabic labels lose their dots and marks inside buttons, chips and table rows, and the riyal sign renders as tofu on an invoicing screen. The scripts pass, because none of them measures glyph extents.

topic: Colour and design systems
where: design-theory.md Part B and Part D (Palette); design-systems.md §2–§7; scripts/palette.mjs, contrast.mjs; templates/SYSTEM.md; dataviz.md §5; resources/type-and-colour.md "Colour tools", "Data palettes"
quote: Steps 11 and 12 are *solved*, not guessed: the darkest lightness that reaches APCA Lc 60 and WCAG 4.5:1 (step 11) / Lc 90 and 7:1 (step 12) against step 2
gap: Nothing enforces that components use only semantic tokens, such as stylelint rules against raw colours and px values; the only check is audit.mjs's count of distinct values. Also missing: a multi-brand or multi-theme architecture (swapping the semantic layer per sub-brand or tenant, with contrast validated per theme in CI); build-pipeline guidance beyond naming Style Dictionary and Terrazzo; color-mix() and relative colour syntax for state tokens, and contrast of translucent overlays; documentation and visual tests for the component layer, as Storybook provides.
risk: After hand-off, raw hex values creep back and a second theme or dark mode breaks on unmapped values. Nothing in CI catches it.

topic: Accessibility baseline (WCAG 2.2) for conventional UI
where: accessibility.md (all sections); ui-ux.md §8; technical-qa.md "Accessibility"; scripts/a11y.mjs (WCAG SCs per section), widgets.mjs, audit.mjs (axe), states.mjs --axe
quote: axe alone raised 35–40%; four rule engines together (axe, HTML_CodeSniffer, Lighthouse, IBM Equal Access) raised 55% as failures; adding the two scripts raised 85%
gap: What remains is real assistive technology. Every check runs in desktop Chromium, so VoiceOver with Safari (iOS and macOS), TalkBack gesture navigation, voice control, switch access and 400% zoom on a real phone are deferred to "a recommended follow-up". Cognitive criteria (3.3.7, 3.3.8, timeouts) are manual only. widgets.mjs covers six contracts (dialog, tabs, disclosure, live, form-errors, menu-button) but not combobox, listbox, grid, tree or slider, which are the widgets custom builds most often get wrong.
risk: A custom combobox or data grid ships with no scripted contract check, and breakage specific to Safari or iOS (list semantics, display: contents, live regions) reaches users because no agent run can observe it.

topic: Generic-AI-aesthetic avoidance
where: SKILL.md commitments 3 and 5; anti-patterns.md (the model's prior, hard bans, purpose-gated table, app-UI tells); art-direction.md §2 and §5; ledger.md + references/ledger/*.jpg; scripts/lib/saturated-fonts.json; audit.mjs generic-look signals; compare.mjs --grid --blur; templates/critique.md
quote: **Similar-brief test:** write one line describing what this plan would look like for a *different* company in the same category. If it is the same plan, it is the prior.
gap: Convergence is judged by eye, from a blurred grid against a handful of the skill's own past outputs in the ledger, and by surface signals (gradient text, card counts, saturated fonts, cliché copy). Nothing measures perceptual distance against a corpus of current generated sites or category competitors. The shortlists in type-and-colour.md could become the next default: the file warns about this, but nothing tracks how often runs pick from them.
risk: A third-generation house style forms across runs (for example, shortlist grotesks + OKLCH-tinted neutrals + a drawn glyph layer). It passes every signal, because the detectors encode only the earlier generations.
